expected with breaking waves up to 16 feet.

* WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National
Seashore and San Francisco Peninsula Coast Counties.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous conditions are forecast along the shoreline.

properties.instruction:

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 12 at 2:53PM PDT until October 12 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.4 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, increased risk of rip currents and sneaker waves
expected with breaking waves up to 16 feet.

* WHERE...San Francisco, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern
Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 3 PM PDT Tuesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 10 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical. Dangerous conditions are
forecast along the shoreline. Hazards include sneaker waves,
strong rip currents, and large breaking waves.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 1:14 PM
Tuesday 10/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.areaDesc: Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 12 at 1:04PM PDT until October 13 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and elevated surf are expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding can be expected
near times of high tide.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 PM PDT this
evening. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Tuesday
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
around high tide at low-lying beach and harbor areas that is
uncommon with normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is
possible. The risk for significant damage is very low. There
is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore. Large
secondary high tides are also expected each evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides are expected to peak around 7.1
to 7.3 feet on Tuesday morning. A Beach Hazards Statement may be
issued on future shifts to follow the Coastal Flood Advisory due
to minor tidal overflow from continued elevated tides and surf
into at least Thursday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 12 at 10:59AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Thursday into the weekend, a series of low pressure systems will
move toward Southeast Alaska, bringing widespread moderate to heavy
rainfall and gale force winds to the Gulf. Strong winds are also
expected for coastal communities. While the exact timing and impacts
of the system are still being refined, confidence is continuing to
increase that this will be a more impactful system for Southeast
Alaska.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the
developing situation and update our forecast.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 12 at 12:54PM EDT until October 12 at 9:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive runoff continues.

* WHERE...Portions of Alexander, Catawba, and Iredell Counties, along
the shores of Lookout Shoals Lake.

* WHEN...Until 900 PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas including
residential yards, docks, and boat-launch areas is ongoing along
the shores of Lookout Shoals Lake. Residents should take immediate
actions to protect property adjacent to the lake and monitor
messaging from county Emergency Management agencies.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1245 PM EDT, Levels of the lakes of the Catawba River remain
elevated as water continues to move downriver following the heavy
rain event over the weekend. While Lookout Shoals Lake has
receded since Sunday afternoon, it remains at Action stage and
some flooding of low-lying areas near the lake shore could
continue through at least this Monday evening.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected. Please obey all barricades and heed any evacuation
orders from local Emergency Management officials.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Northern Coastal Humboldt; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 12 at 3:02AM PDT until October 12 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...A very long period westerly swell will increase the
threat of sneaker waves.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...Through this evening. The risk will increase as winds
weaken.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

NWSheadline: BEACH HAZARDS STATEMENT NOW IN EFFECT THROUGH THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Pohnpei Coastal Waters; Kosrae Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 12 at 1:29PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
As Invest 96W continues to slowly organize and strengthen north of
Kosrae/east of Pohnpei, inflow into the developing disturbance will
allow for locally heavy rainfall to develop, with over 1 inch per
hour rain rates probable from time to time. Rainfall totals will
likely be 2 to 5 inches tonight through Wednesday, with locally
higher amounts possible.

Winds will also increase as 96W strengthens, and at least isolated
wind gusts to 35 knots are possible with any heavy shower or
thunderstorm that develops.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island
boating as the week continues. Also keep up to date with the latest
information from your local emergency management agency.

NWSheadline: LOCALLY HEAVY RAINFALL AND GUSTY WINDS TONIGHT THROUGH WEDNESDAY, POSSIBLY LONGER
